classification_detail: 1 sorry: apm_a96J08 (main theorem). The integral evaluation requires the residue theorem for rectangular contours (boundary integral = 2πi × sum of interior residues). Mathlib has Cauchy-Goursat for rectangles (zero-residue case only, via integral_boundary_rect_eq_zero_of_differentiableOn) but not the residue theorem version needed for poles inside the contour. The informal proof uses a rectangular contour exploiting the 2πi periodicity of e^z, with poles at z=0 and z=2πi contributing via half-residue indentation.

blockers: Residue theorem for rectangles: boundary integral = 2πi × sum of interior residues. Mathlib has integral_boundary_rect_eq_zero_of_differentiableOn (Cauchy-Goursat, no-poles case) but NOT the general residue version needed when a pole (at z=2πi) lies inside the rectangular contour. Excising the pole (removing a small disk) would require proving that the small-circle integral converges to 2πi×residue as radius→0, combined with Cauchy-Goursat on the punctured rectangle. This is substantial topological machinery not available in Mathlib.
